introduction: On this Sunday, Moses tells Israel that no nation has a God so near to it, and laws so just. In the Gospel, Jesus warns against honoring God with our lips while our hearts are far from him: it is what comes from within that makes a person unclean. Saint James asks us to be doers of the word and not hearers only. Let us open our hearts to the word that can save us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God is near to us whenever we call on him. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that her worship may come from the heart and lead to love of God and neighbor. Let us pray to the Lord.
For orphans, widows and all who are alone in their distress: that Christians may visit and care for them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are trapped by evil thoughts, habits or addictions: that God may purify their hearts and set them free. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who teach the faith: that they may hand on God's word faithfully, without adding to it or taking from it. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be doers of the word and not hearers only. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, every good gift comes from you. Purify our hearts, so that our worship may be true and our lives may bear the fruit of your word. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Near to us in heart
reflection.body:
Moses wants Israel to see their law as a gift and a sign of God's nearness: "For what great nation is there that has a god so near to them as the LORD our God is whenever we call on him?" The commandments are not meant to be a burden but a way of living wisely in God's presence.

In the Gospel, the Pharisees criticize Jesus' disciples for eating without the ritual washing of hands. Jesus answers with words from Isaiah: "This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me." Religion can become a matter of outward habits while the heart stays untouched.

Then Jesus teaches the crowd something radical: "There is nothing from outside of the man that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man." He lists what comes from the heart: "evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts, covetings, wickedness, deceit." The real battle is inside us.

Saint James brings it down to daily life: "be doers of the word, and not only hearers." And he gives a simple test of true religion: "to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world." Faith shows itself in care for the most vulnerable.

Our traditions and practices are precious when they express a living faith. This week, take a few minutes each evening to look honestly at your heart: what thoughts and desires came out of it today? Ask God to purify it. And choose one concrete act of care for someone who is alone.
